profile.lede: I build software that works long after launch day.

paragraphs.t: — backend architecture in Django and PostgreSQL, frontend systems in React, and the infrastructure that keeps them running
Good software is judged after release, not before it. I build
— maintainable, clearly structured, and built around real constraints from the first commit.
Most of my work sits at the intersection of
, and frontend engineering — solving problems that span the entire stack, not just one layer of it.

items.description: At Azem, I develop and maintain production-ready full-stack web applications built with Django and React, designing scalable REST APIs and secure authentication systems alongside PostgreSQL and MySQL database structures. Day-to-day, that also means managing Linux VPS infrastructure — configuring Nginx, Gunicorn, domains, SSL certificates, and production deployments — and maintaining secure hosting environments with reliable backup strategies.

As a Computer Engineer Intern, I developed a real-time data acquisition system, contributed to UI/UX implementation, and worked through a mix of hardware and software issues — documenting each solution along the way.
I maintained operational reporting across large datasets, working closely in Excel and Google Sheets to keep every figure accurate and every report dependable.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: A closer look at the systems I've built, from backend architecture to production deployments.

items.title: AARC
items.subtitle: Four role-specific workspaces operating on one recruitment and rental-management backend.

overview.t: AARC is a production recruitment platform coordinating the full workflow across
four independent dashboards

: employees, external offices, administration, and rental administration. A shared Django REST Framework backend centralizes authentication, records, workflow transitions, and permissions while each React dashboard exposes only the actions relevant to its role.

architecture.frontend: React dashboards with role-aware navigation, forms, operational queues, and shared API clients
architecture.backend: Django REST Framework with authentication, permission policies, workflow endpoints, and administration services
architecture.database: MySQL relational database for users, recruitment records, rental operations, and workflow state
architecture.deployment: Linux VPS with Nginx as reverse proxy and Gunicorn serving the Django application

highlights: Four dashboards tailored to employees, external offices, administrators, and rental administrators
Central authentication with role-based authorization enforced by the API
Recruitment records move through controlled operational states instead of disconnected manual updates
Production stack operated on a self-managed Linux VPS
challenges: Allowing four dashboards to share one backend without leaking records or actions between roles
Keeping workflow transitions consistent when different teams update the same recruitment process
Operating the React and Django services reliably on a self-managed production server
solutions: Placed authorization in reusable DRF permission policies and scoped every query to the authenticated role
Modeled recruitment stages as validated backend transitions so dashboards cannot create invalid workflow states
Separated static delivery, reverse proxying, and application serving across Nginx and Gunicorn with repeatable server configuration

items.title: Shahm Law
items.subtitle: A law-firm website backed by a custom publishing, request, and communication system.

overview.t: Shahm Law combines a public legal-services website with a
purpose-built content management system
. The administration dashboard manages site content, team access, newsletter subscribers and campaigns, contact enquiries, service requests, and internal notifications from one controlled workspace.

architecture.frontend: Public service pages plus a protected administration dashboard for content, requests, and communications
architecture.backend: Custom CMS and application services for publishing, role management, newsletters, notifications, and request processing
architecture.database: Relational content and operations model linking pages, subscribers, enquiries, service requests, users, and notifications
architecture.deployment: Production web deployment at shamlaw.sa with integrated email-delivery workflows

highlights: Editors publish structured website content without code changes
Newsletter subscriptions and outbound campaigns are managed inside the administration system
Contact enquiries and service requests enter separate operational queues
Role management limits publishing, communication, and request-handling capabilities
challenges: Combining editorial work and client-service operations without creating an unstructured dashboard
Sending newsletters while preserving subscriber state and preventing duplicate campaigns
Keeping public forms open while protecting the administrative workflow behind them
solutions: Separated content, subscribers, enquiries, and service requests into focused modules sharing one access model
Built campaign and recipient state into the newsletter workflow so sends can be tracked and guarded
Validated public submissions through dedicated endpoints and exposed them only to authorized roles

items.title: KneeGuide
items.subtitle: A connected rehabilitation prototype that turns Arduino knee-angle readings into clinical exercise records.

overview.t: KneeGuide connects a React healthcare interface to an Arduino measurement device over Bluetooth. During assigned exercises, the platform captures
real-time knee-angle measurements
, presents them to the patient, and stores session results for doctors to review through reports, progress analytics, appointments, and exercise-management tools.

architecture.frontend: React doctor and patient dashboards with Bluetooth pairing, live angle visualization, assignments, reports, and progress views
architecture.backend: Django services for accounts, clinical relationships, exercise plans, appointments, measurement sessions, and reporting
architecture.database: Django-managed relational model for patients, doctors, assignments, appointments, sessions, and angle observations
architecture.deployment: Research web prototype at knee.fyaa.io paired with an Arduino-based Bluetooth measurement device

highlights: Doctor workspace for assigning exercises and reviewing session-level reports
Patient workspace for appointments, assigned routines, Bluetooth pairing, and guided measurements
Live angle visualization converts hardware readings into feedback during movement
Progress tracking compares completed sessions instead of relying only on manual notes
challenges: Maintaining a usable Bluetooth session when packets arrive intermittently or the connection drops
Synchronizing measurements with the correct patient, exercise, repetition, and session
Presenting movement data clearly without overwhelming users with raw samples
solutions: Introduced an explicit pairing lifecycle with connection state, validation, and recoverable disconnect handling
Normalized angle observations before attaching them to the active exercise session
Separated live feedback from summarized reports while preserving detailed readings for analysis

items.title: TripSplit
items.subtitle: A shared trip ledger for joining groups, recording expenses, and tracking the remaining budget.

overview.t: TripSplit gives a travel group one shared financial record. A trip owner creates the trip and distributes an
invite code
; members join the same workspace, record expenses, and see spending and remaining budget update from the group ledger rather than maintaining separate calculations.

architecture.frontend: Responsive trip workspace for creation, code-based joining, member management, expenses, and budget summaries
architecture.backend: Application service enforcing trip membership, invite-code access, expense ownership, and budget calculations
architecture.database: Relational ledger connecting trips, members, invite codes, budgets, and expense entries

highlights: Invite codes let travelers join the correct trip without manual account coordination
Every expense is attached to the shared trip and the member who recorded it
Remaining budget is derived from one ledger so every member sees the same total
Trip owners manage membership while participants continue recording costs
challenges: Preventing invite codes from granting access to unrelated trips
Keeping totals consistent when several members add or revise expenses
Representing membership and expense ownership without duplicating trip data per user
solutions: Resolved and validated codes server-side before creating a scoped membership
Calculated budget summaries from authoritative expense records instead of client totals
Modeled trips, memberships, and expenses separately so one ledger serves every participant

items.title: Dorina Pro
items.subtitle: A browser-based football tournament engine for league and knockout competitions.

overview.t: Dorina Pro manages football tournaments entirely in the browser. Organizers choose league or knockout mode, enter teams and results, and the application derives
standings, qualifiers, winners, and the final top three
from tournament state persisted in LocalStorage.

architecture.frontend: Single-page tournament interface with separate league and knockout calculation flows
architecture.backend: None; tournament rules and progression are executed in the browser
architecture.database: LocalStorage persistence for teams, fixtures, results, standings, and tournament progress

highlights: League tables recalculate points and ordering as match results change
Knockout rounds advance winners automatically through the bracket
Tournament state survives refreshes without accounts or a remote database
Completion logic announces the champion and final top-three positions
challenges: Supporting league and knockout rules without mixing incompatible progression models
Reconstructing a valid tournament after a browser refresh
Handling edited results without leaving standings or winners stale
solutions: Isolated each competition mode behind deterministic calculation functions
Serialized minimal tournament state and recomputed derived views when loading
Made standings and advancement derived data so edits trigger a consistent recalculation

items.title: Student Results
items.subtitle: A lightweight result lookup that reads synchronized student records directly from Google Sheets.

overview.t: Student Results replaces a custom application server with
Google Sheets as the maintained data source
. Staff continue updating familiar spreadsheets while students search the synchronized records through a focused frontend using their identifying information.

architecture.frontend: Search interface that validates student input, queries the published dataset, and presents the matching result
architecture.backend: No custom backend; Google Sheets provides the managed record source
architecture.database: Google Sheets rows containing synchronized student result records

highlights: Staff update results through their existing spreadsheet workflow
The frontend reads synchronized records without a separately maintained API server
Student-information search narrows access to the requested record
The small deployment surface keeps operational overhead low
challenges: Using a spreadsheet as a live source while keeping lookup behavior predictable
Normalizing cells with inconsistent spacing, casing, or number formatting
Avoiding unnecessary infrastructure for a narrowly scoped read-only workflow
solutions: Added normalization before comparing search fields with sheet values
Kept the flow read-only and treated the spreadsheet as the single maintained source
Used a static client architecture independent of a custom application server

items.title: Terhal
items.subtitle: A bilingual, multi-page website for presenting a non-profit organization’s work and programs.

overview.t: Terhal is a React website spanning more than ten Arabic and English pages. It organizes the organization’s identity, programs, and public information into a shared
bilingual page system
that adapts navigation, reading direction, and responsive layouts across both languages.

architecture.frontend: React component system shared across more than ten Arabic and English pages
architecture.backend: None; public information is delivered as a frontend-only website
architecture.database: None; page content is bundled with the site
architecture.deployment: Static deployment on Netlify at terhalv1.netlify.app

highlights: More than ten pages share consistent navigation and reusable sections
Arabic layouts switch reading direction without maintaining a separate site
Both languages preserve the same information hierarchy
Responsive behavior covers dense internal pages and the landing experience
challenges: Keeping navigation and structure synchronized across two languages and many routes
Supporting RTL and LTR without duplicating every component
Maintaining readable hierarchy across mobile and desktop breakpoints
solutions: Centralized route and navigation definitions for both languages
Built shared React sections with direction-aware layout rules
Defined responsive behavior at component level for consistency across long-form pages

items.title: OQOL
items.subtitle: A tailored WordPress implementation that gives the client direct control over routine content updates.

overview.t: OQOL is a WordPress implementation customized around the client’s page and publishing requirements. WordPress acts as the operational content layer so the team can
maintain pages without developer intervention
while the public presentation remains constrained to the approved structure.

architecture.frontend: Customized WordPress theme and page templates aligned with the client’s content structure
architecture.backend: WordPress administration with configured editing controls and media management
architecture.database: WordPress relational content store for pages, settings, and media references

highlights: Templates reflect required content types instead of exposing a blank page builder
Routine copy and media changes are handled through WordPress administration
Reusable content patterns keep repeated sections consistent
The implementation stays within familiar WordPress operations for handover
challenges: Adapting editing flexibility to a fixed client-approved presentation
Preventing routine content changes from breaking page structure
Keeping administration simple for editors who do not work with code
solutions: Mapped recurring content into constrained templates and reusable fields
Limited editing choices to the controls needed for each page type
Configured the CMS around the client’s publishing workflow

items.title: CodeDuo
items.subtitle: A corporate services website that turns software capabilities into a clear enquiry path.

overview.t: CodeDuo presents software-development services through a responsive corporate frontend. The information architecture moves from capability areas to service detail and contact actions using
consistent branded components
rather than unrelated landing-page sections.

architecture.frontend: Responsive component-based website for service pages, company information, and enquiry paths
architecture.backend: No application backend required for the public presentation layer
architecture.database: None; corporate content is delivered with the frontend

highlights: Service categories are structured around specific software-delivery capabilities
Repeated patterns create continuity between overview and service detail
Contact actions remain accessible across desktop and mobile layouts
Typography, spacing, and color rules are reusable frontend primitives
challenges: Explaining several technical service lines without creating a dense catalogue
Maintaining one visual system across differently sized sections
Preserving clear enquiry paths on small screens
solutions: Grouped offerings by client problem and delivery outcome
Created shared section, typography, and spacing primitives
Placed responsive contact actions at deliberate decision points

items.title: Social
items.subtitle: An open-source, bilingual link hub designed for self-hosting and custom identity.

overview.t: Social is a self-hostable alternative to hosted link-in-bio services. It packages profile details, destinations, bilingual content, and visual identity into a
small deployable frontend
that can be branded and published without depending on a subscription platform.

architecture.frontend: Responsive bilingual link page with configurable profile, destinations, and branding
architecture.backend: None required for the core project
architecture.database: Configuration-based content; no database service required
architecture.deployment: Static, self-hostable build with a live instance at social.fyaa.io

highlights: Arabic and English profiles are delivered from one lightweight codebase
Brand colors, identity, and destination links can be replaced without rebuilding the layout
No third-party link-platform account is required
Static output deploys to simple hosting with minimal operational cost
challenges: Keeping customization approachable without a full administration backend
Making the compact layout work naturally in RTL and LTR
Keeping the page fast when opened from mobile social applications
solutions: Separated profile content and brand settings from presentation components
Used direction-aware rules so one component tree supports both languages
Avoided server-side dependencies to keep deployment small
